findings.evidence: Book p. 39, §3.3.3: "The compute savings are straightforward: if only na = 12.8B of nt = 47B total parameters are active per token, the FLOP count drops by the active fraction relative to a same-size dense model."
findings.issue: Arithmetically incorrect phrasing: 'drops by the active fraction' means subtracting the active fraction (27%), yielding 73% of original FLOPs — which is wrong. The actual result is that FLOPs drop TO 27% of a same-size dense model (12.8/47 ≈ 27%), i.e., a 73% reduction. 'By' and 'to' yield different numbers: by 27% gives 0.73×, to 27% gives 0.27×. The intended meaning is 'to.'
findings.fix_instruction: Change 'drops by the active fraction' to 'drops to the active fraction' (or equivalently, 'is reduced to 27% of the same-size dense model's FLOP count').

findings.evidence: PDF p. 71: "The dense-70B column traces to the canonical scenario (Ch 4, Table 4-2); the MoE column is an [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] worked variant, not a measurement claim." | Rows in the same MoE column, PDF p. 70: "active params per token | 70B | ~12.8B | top-2 from 8 = 2/8 = 25% of expert mass ≈ 11.4B + ~1.4B always-on = 12.8B [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]" and "KV cache per request (9.2K ctx, FP16) | ~24.1 GB | ~1.2 GB | ... [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]" | PDF p. 58, Table 3-2: "Total parameters (across 8 experts) | ~47B | ~5.7B per expert × 8 = 45.6B + ~1.4B always-on = 47B [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]"
findings.issue: The table-level note blanket-labels the whole MoE column [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION], while four rows inside that same column carry [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]. The Preface is explicit that 'ASSUMPTION/DERIVED says whether a number was chosen or computed'. The same ~47B total is [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] in Table 3-2 (PDF p. 58) but [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] in Table 3-3's 'total parameters' row (PDF p. 69), so one quantity carries two different epistemic tags eleven pages apart.
findings.fix_instruction: Change the Table 3-3 closing note to say the MoE column carries [ILLUSTRATIVE] provenance with per-row ASSUMPTION/DERIVED status (rather than asserting the whole column is [ASSUMPTION]), and make the ~47B row's tag agree with Table 3-2 — it is computed from the component sum, so it should read [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] in both tables.

findings.evidence: PDF p. 53: "The paper-by-paper treatment — corruption processes, masked samplers, flow matching, cache boundaries — is carried in Appendix A's alternative-inference note, citations with it." and "The full treatment is in Appendix A." | PDF p. 65: "The implementation-level inspection (which function picks the expert, and what offload costs) is in Appendix A's alternative-inference note."
findings.issue: Three separate cross-references to Appendix A are given without naming the target's subsection, figure or table number, even though Appendix A is organized into lettered subsections (A.1–A.6+ per the Preface) and the book's stated convention is '§ chapter.section'. 'Appendix A's alternative-inference note' is a descriptive handle, not a resolvable pointer; a reader cannot tell whether the material is in A.1, A.5 or a boxed note, and 'The full treatment is in Appendix A' points at a 33-page appendix rather than a location.
findings.fix_instruction: Name the subsection for each pointer — e.g. 'Appendix A § A.6 (alternative-inference note)' — and add the subsection number to the Contents entry for Appendix A so the pointer resolves; likewise cite the specific figure/table where one carries the material.

findings.evidence: Ch 7 p.147: 'Any inference residency after* fine-tuning is a separate weights+KV question, priced by Table 7-1.)*'; Ch 3 p.67: 'their resident* weight (2 × 11.4 GB = 22.8 GB…)' with the closing marker on p.69: 'holds the same ~0.6 GB.*'; Ch 4 p.78: 'a mid-tier* managed-API list price' with the closing marker 'the full walk-through is §4.3.)*'. No footnote text is anchored to any of these markers, whereas the book does anchor asterisk footnotes correctly elsewhere (e.g. Ch 4 p.83 sidebar: '≈ $24.97 *' → '* Peak-provisioned capacity ÷ average…').
findings.issue: Orphaned/misplaced asterisk markers: an asterisk opens mid-phrase after words that are not footnoted terms ('after', 'resident', 'mid-tier') and closes after the block's final period with no note text — broken emphasis or a dangling footnote marker.
findings.fix_instruction: Remove the orphaned asterisks or convert them to proper footnotes with anchored markers and note text (e.g. footnote the ~23 GB rounding of the two active experts' resident weight and the mid-tier vs frontier API price tier).
